before.label: English
before.title: Even Stone Could Have Melted
stanzas: As the world reached the moon, I too could have reached it;
if hard work were valued, my sweat too could have shone.
The days somehow passed, but the nights passed in loneliness;
had you come with the memories, the night too could have stirred.
You called my heart a stone; let it be stone, then.
Had you rested your head upon my chest, even stone could have melted.
Though I drank many a tavern dry, my feet never wavered;
had you held out your hand to steady me, I too could have staggered.
Now I go about writing stories of heart-deceiving relationships;
had you stood by me a little, I could have written a ghazal of fidelity.
In January my body burns like June;
had you kissed my forehead, even the fever could have fallen.
